podcast.title: First Management Client (1981) – The U-Men
podcast.body: Susan Silver began her career in artist management by managing The U-Men, a Seattle group formed in 1981 that predated the widespread Grunge movement by a couple of years. She also managed Screaming Trees before taking on Soundgarden. "Silver got her start managing the U-Men, a Seattle group that predated the whole Grunge thing by a couple of years in 1981."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Marriage to Chris Cornell (September 1990) – Manager and Wife
podcast.body: Susan Silver, who was already managing Soundgarden, began dating Chris Cornell and they married in September 1990. Their relationship lasted through significant periods in the rise of both Soundgarden and Alice in Chains, as well as Chris's early solo career and personal struggles. "She and Chris started dating, which probably had its awkward moments with the rest of the band, and then they got married in September of 1990."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Divorce from Chris Cornell (2004) – Followed by Lawsuit
podcast.body: Susan Silver and Chris Cornell divorced in 2004, after a relationship that spanned the rise of Soundgarden and Alice in Chains, Soundgarden's breakup, Cornell's initial solo career, and his struggles with addiction, as well as the death of Alice in Chains singer Lane Staley. Their divorce was followed by a contentious lawsuit initiated by Cornell. "She and Chris divorced in 2004."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Atmosphere Artist Management (2005-2011) – Post-Divorce Venture
podcast.body: After her divorce from Chris Cornell, Susan Silver established a new company called Atmosphere Artist Management in 2005. This venture, however, was later shut down in 2011 for unspecified reasons. "Susan created a new company called Atmosphere Artist Management in 2005, but it was shut down for some reason in 2011."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Co-Manager of Alice in Chains – Partnership with Kelly Curtis
podcast.body: Susan Silver co-managed Alice in Chains with Kelly Curtis through their shared management company. When Mother Love Bone collapsed and transformed into Pearl Jam, Kelly Curtis shifted his focus to become Pearl Jam's full-time manager, leaving Susan to manage Alice in Chains independently. "When Mother Lovebone started to get hot, Kelly wanted to spend more time with them. Meanwhile, Ken wanted out, so Susan and Kelly became co-managers of Allison Chains through their own management company."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lawsuit by Chris Cornell – Alleged Royalties Diversion and Withholding of Items
podcast.body: Following their 2004 divorce, Chris Cornell sued Susan Silver for a million dollars, accusing her of diverting Soundgarden royalties to the other band members and withholding valuable items such as a guitar, Grammy Awards, demo tapes, personal recordings, diaries, and journals. The suit used strong terms like "fraud, oppression, and malice" in its documentation, and it was eventually settled. "Chris sued Susan for a million dollars, claiming that she diverted Soundgarden royalties away from him and to the other three band members, words like fraud, oppression, and malice reused in the documents."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Seattle Group Predating Grunge (1981) – First Client of Susan Silver
xref.body: The U-Men were a Seattle group that formed in 1981, predating the mainstream emergence of grunge by a few years. They were the first band managed by Susan Silver, who later became a prominent manager in the Seattle music scene for bands like Soundgarden and Alice in Chains. "Silver got her start managing the U-Men, a Seattle group that predated the whole Grunge thing by a couple of years in 1981."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Management by Susan Silver (1983)
xref.body: Susan Silver began managing bands in the Seattle area in 1983, soon after running the door at an all-ages club called the Metropolis. The U-Men were one of her initial clients, representing a "pre-grunge" band in the burgeoning Seattle scene.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Managed by Susan Silver (1983)
xref.body: Screaming Trees were an early client of Susan Silver, who started managing bands in Seattle in 1983 while still majoring in Chinese at the University of Washington. This management role predated her work with Soundgarden and Alice in Chains.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Management by Susan Silver (1985-1998)
xref.body: Susan Silver started managing Soundgarden in 1985, formalizing the arrangement by 1986. Her initial motivation was a "starry-eyed idea of helping bands reach their dreams." Silver continued to manage the band until 1998, a year after their 1997 breakup, at which point she shut down her company, Silver Management.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Marriage to Chris Cornell (1990)
xref.body: Susan Silver began dating Soundgarden's singer, Chris Cornell, about a year before she formally managed the band. They married in 1990 and, initially, their personal and professional lives were successfully kept separate, with many Soundgarden fans unaware that the singer was married to the manager.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Soundgarden Breakup (1997) – Tension from Manager/Wife Susan Silver and Separate Tour Transport
xref.body: The band broke up in 1997 partly due to the unresolvable conflict of interest created by Cornell being married to Susan Silver, who was also the band's manager (and the manager of Alice in Chains and Screaming Trees). By the end of the band's existence, each member was reportedly traveling separately by their own bus or plane between shows. After the divorce in 2002, Cornell filed a complaint with the California Labor Commission in 2006 alleging Silver had performed booking work without the required talent agent's license, and sought return of money she made from Soundgarden activities in 2005. "No conflict of interest there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Discovery of Death (April 19, 2002)
xref.body: On April 17, 2002, Lane Staley's mother visited his apartment to inform him of Demri's brother's death, finding unopened mail and no answer at the door. Two days later, his accountants alerted Alice in Chains' former manager, Susan Silver, that no money had been withdrawn for two weeks, a significant red flag. Silver contacted Staley's mother, who returned to the condo, found his usually quiet cat, Sadie, meowing excessively, and then called 911. Police forced entry and discovered Staley's body amidst drug paraphernalia. "On April 19, the accountants who looked after Lane's money contacted Alison Chains former manager Susan Silver, saying that no money had been withdrawn from his bank account for two weeks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Layne Staley's Death and Discovery (April 5-19, 2002)
xref.body: Layne Staley died around Friday, April 5, 2002, an anniversary date shared with Kurt Cobain's death. His body was discovered on April 19, 2002, after his mother became concerned. On April 17, she found a pile of uncollected mail outside his condo. Two days later, accountants informed his former manager, Susan Silver, that no money had been withdrawn from his bank account for two weeks. When his mother returned to the condo and heard his usually quiet cat, Sadie, meowing excessively, she called 911. Police broke in and found Staley's body with drug paraphernalia scattered nearby; an autopsy determined he had been dead for approximately two weeks. "The autopsy deterrent that he'd been dead for about two weeks, probably dying on Friday, April 5, the day after Mike Stars visit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Divorce Litigation (2003)
xref.body: After Chris Cornell and Susan Silver divorced in 2003, a lawsuit ensued. Chris sued for $1 million in damages, alleging that Silver, as Soundgarden's manager, diverted money owed to him to other band members. The suit also claimed she withheld his guitars, demos, journals, notes, and two Grammy Awards statues, and sought to permanently bar her from representing Soundgarden due to "irreconcilable conflicts of interest," which explained the delay in a Soundgarden reunion.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lawsuit Against Ex-Wife Susan Silver (2004) – Royalties and Possessions Dispute
xref.body: After divorcing Susan Silver in 2004, Chris Cornell sued her for a million dollars. He claimed she diverted Soundgarden royalties to the other band members and withheld valuable items, including a guitar, Grammy Awards, demo tapes, personal recordings, diaries, and journals. This legal dispute was cited as a reason for the prolonged delay in the Soundgarden reunion, although everything was eventually settled. "Chris sued Susan for a million dollars, claiming that she diverted Soundgarden royalties away from him and to the other three band members, words like fraud, oppression, and malice reused in the documents."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Advice from Susan Silver
xref.body: When Nirvana needed advice regarding a record contract, they approached Susan Silver. Although she had the opportunity to manage them, Silver ultimately declined the offer.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Co-Management and Susan Silver's Involvement
xref.body: Alice in Chains was initially co-managed by Kelly Curtis. When Curtis became distracted by the growing popularity of his other band, Mother Love Bone, Susan Silver took over much of the day-to-day management for Alice in Chains. It was Silver who secured their record deal.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kelly Curtis's Managerial Focus
xref.body: Kelly Curtis became fully "tied up and running the life" of Pearl Jam, a development that meant he no longer had time to manage Alice in Chains. This shift in focus led to Susan Silver becoming Alice in Chains' sole manager.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lane Staley's Death – Impact on Susan Silver
xref.body: The death of Alice in Chains singer Lane Staley was a significant event that occurred during Susan Silver's management tenure and personal relationship with Chris Cornell. This tragic loss was mentioned in the context of the difficulties Silver faced leading up to her divorce from Cornell. "Not to mention the total implosion and death of Allison Chains singer Lane Staley."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Managed by Susan Silver and Kelly Curtis – Early Co-Management
xref.body: Alice in Chains was initially managed by Susan Silver, Chris Cornell's ex-wife, in partnership with Kelly Curtis. When Curtis shifted his focus to manage Pearl Jam, Silver took on sole management responsibilities for Alice in Chains, navigating the band through challenges including singer Lane Staley's death. "Kelly and his buddy Ken managed Allison Chains. When Mother Lovebone started to get hot, Kelly wanted to spend more time with them. Meanwhile, Ken wanted out, so Susan and Kelly became co-managers of Allison Chains through their own management company."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Manager Kelly Curtis's Distraction
xref.body: Kelly Curtis, who initially co-managed Alice in Chains, became distracted by the growing popularity of Mother Love Bone, his other management client. This distraction led to Susan Silver taking on more day-to-day responsibilities for Alice in Chains.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reunion Delay – Linked to Lawsuit
xref.body: The legal dispute between Chris Cornell and his ex-wife and former manager, Susan Silver, regarding alleged diverted royalties and withheld band property, contributed to the delay in Soundgarden's reunion. This conflict involved claims of fraud, oppression, and malice. "So if you've ever wondered why it took so long for the Soundgarden reunion to come together, there's part of your answer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Susan Silver Becomes Sole Manager
xref.body: When Kelly Curtis became fully engaged in managing Pearl Jam, he no longer had time for Alice in Chains, leading Susan Silver to become their sole manager. Silver maintains a close relationship with the band, describing them as "like brothers" to her, having shared extreme life experiences, both good and bad.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Susan Silver as Manager – Ex-Wife and Business Partner
xref.body: Susan Silver, Chris Cornell's ex-wife, served as the manager for Soundgarden. Her role as manager became a point of contention after their divorce in 2004 when Cornell sued her over alleged diverted royalties and disputed ownership of band-related items. "She is also the ex-manager of Soundgarden and Allison Chains."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
